subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw accept this combined canonical-readiness and hosting-profile architecture as v1, or split plugin providers, activation identity, operator profiles, and release conformance into later acceptance stages?
rationale: The proposal is technically coherent and strongly proven, but it creates permanent public API, configuration, readiness-failure, and support promises whose accepted scope requires explicit cross-area maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept a bounded combined v1
options.body: Approve core condition normalization and only the minimum provider, profile, and activation surface needed for the first supported hosting contracts.

options.title: Split into staged RFCs
options.body: Accept core readiness normalization first and separately review plugin providers, operator profiles, activation identity, and release gating.

options.title: Continue targeted fixes
options.body: Decline canonical hosting profiles and address individual readiness gaps through existing Gateway and diagnostic surfaces.

recommendation.title: Accept a bounded combined v1
recommendation.body: Approve core condition normalization and only the minimum provider, profile, and activation surface needed for the first supported hosting contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest recent current-main history across the Gateway, plugin, configuration, health, and startup surfaces affected by the architecture choice.
